_comment: Written by the trading runs (9:30a / hourly / 3:30p ET). Never contains account numbers, broker IDs, or any account other than the sandbox.

account.note: FLAT on a live read taken by this run at the open, and this is the first Monday the board has opened with a balance that can pay for a position outright. The open slot fired 09:41 ET against 09:33, eight minutes late and comfortably inside the staleness guard - which is the difference between today and 8/7, when the same slot arrived 143 minutes late and the guard stopped it dead. The scope preflight matched the target account exactly against the connector list and every other account was discarded unread. The broker returns zero equity positions, zero option positions, 109.88 of settled cash and 109.88 of buying power with nothing unsettled. Sixth identical read in a row, and it was taken rather than copied: positions come from the broker and never from this file. The balance still traces to the SMR round trip closed 8/6 - bought 2 at 0.55 and 0.59 for 114.00, sold at 0.49 for 98.00, -16.00 or -14.0% - which settled T+1 on 8/7 and has sat unspent through the weekend because the only slot entitled to spend it missed its window.
account.openingNote: THIS IS THE OPENING READ AND THE DAILY ENTRY MANDATE IS DISCHARGED, forced on item 1: buy 12 JOBY at a 8.85 limit, target 10.62, stop 8.14, time stop the 8/14 close, expiring 10:30 ET. Exits were checked before entries and there was nothing to check - a flat book means no target, no stop, no time stop and no option expiry no-fly window was due, and none went unenforced. Two things this run settled that were handed to it by name. FIRST, the straddle Friday's pre-close owed to this slot was pulled: the SMCI 8/14 32 call marks 2.51 against a 2.05 put, a 4.56 straddle on a 32.21 spot, so the market prices a 14.2% move on tomorrow night's print. SMCI is refused on that arithmetic and not on a view - the rulebook stops equity at -8%, and an 8% stop sits entirely inside a 14.2% expected move, so the realistic bad case gaps through the stop rather than filling at it and the exit written before entry would not be the exit taken. That matters beyond the refusal, because SMCI was the ONLY name on this board with a forward catalyst, and once it is gone item 1 cannot be passed anywhere on the list. SECOND, options were priced before any thesis was built, as the 8/5 rule requires, and are refused for a third consecutive session on SPREAD rather than affordability: eight contracts quoted live across JOBY, SOUN and SMR at 3-6 weeks, every one clearing the 0.40 delta floor, several affordable outright, and the tightest of them at 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling. Three different cash balances - 128.90, 126.06 and now 109.88 - have produced the same answer, which is the point at which it stops being about the balance. The tape reversed wholesale over the weekend: breadth is 10 RED of 12 after six consecutive 10-green reads on Friday, and the names that extended hardest into Friday's bell are the ones being unwound hardest now. JOBY is one of two green names and the only green one without a print tomorrow. That is the entry, and it is also exactly what is wrong with it - relative strength on a red tape is a real condition and it is not a catalyst, so item 1 is marked fail and the entry is published forced rather than dressed up as something cleaner.

entryWatch.setup: JOBY post-earnings continuation - SPECIFICATION PUBLISHED, forced on item 1
entryWatch.trigger: Live: buy 12 JOBY at a 8.85 limit, target 10.62, stop 8.14, time stop the 8/14 close. Expires 10:30 ET and a human executes it - this run has no order authority.
entryWatch.why: The first thing a reader should see, and it is marked forced so it reads as what it is. JOBY reported 8/5 after the close; 8/6 was the reaction bar, gapping from a 7.80 close to an 8.15 open and closing 8.23 on 49.4M shares against a month averaging roughly 35M; 8/7 continued to 8.64 on 33.6M. Today it is 8.82 bid against 8.84, +2.1%, through Friday's 8.72 high, on a morning when the complex it trades with is being sold. ITEM 1 FAILS and is not argued into a pass: the 8/5 print is three sessions old and priced, the rulebook names day-2 continuation and this is day 3, and there is no catalyst of any kind inside a five-session hold. What is true instead is that JOBY is holding and extending a post-earnings advance while OKLO gives back 7.7%, SOUN 6.1%, SMR 4.8% and IONQ 4.0% - relative strength on a red tape, which is a genuine condition and is still not an answer to why does this move meaningfully, soon. That distinction is the whole reason this is forced. Exits are struck off the limit: +20% is 10.62, -8% is 8.14, and the stop sits 0.71 below entry against a name whose recent daily range runs 0.38 to 0.67, so it is roughly one session of noise rather than inside it. Twelve shares is 106.20 of 109.88 deployable, one position of a two-position ceiling. If it fills below 8.85 the operator should re-strike both exits off the actual fill.

entryWatch.setup: SMCI pre-earnings - REFUSED on its own straddle, and the number is finally written down
entryWatch.trigger: None. The 8/14 32-strike straddle prices a 14.2% move on the 8/11 print, and an 8% stop cannot survive it.
entryWatch.why: The open item Friday's pre-close handed to this slot by name, and it is discharged rather than carried forward again. The at-the-money straddle was pulled live: the SMCI 2026-08-14 32 call marks 2.51 - 2.47 bid against 2.55, on 2,399 open interest - and the 32 put marks 2.05 - 2.00 bid against 2.10, on 645 open interest - for a 4.56 straddle against a 32.21 spot at the moment it was struck. That is a 14.2% implied move on tomorrow night's report. The refusal follows from the number rather than from any view about the company: the rulebook stops equity at -8%, an 8% stop sits entirely inside a 14.2% expected move, and so the realistic bad case is a gap straight through the stop rather than a fill at it. An exit that the event is priced to jump is not an exit, which is the sense in which item 3 is a real gate and not a formality. An option here is refused twice over and was never reachable: any 3-6 week expiry necessarily spans 8/11, and the rulebook forbids holding an option through a print outright. Worth stating plainly because it shaped everything after it - SMCI is the only name on this board with a catalyst ahead, so eliminating it is what left item 1 unpassable and made today's entry a forced one rather than a clean one. SMCI is 32.52 bid, +4.5%, being bid up into the print, which is also item 5's warning in its textbook form. The estimate re-verified on the live calendar today reads 0.88 against the 0.69 this board has carried since 8/7; the live calendar is the authority and the row was corrected to it.

entryWatch.setup: The speculative complex - Friday reversed wholesale over the weekend
entryWatch.trigger: No level. Item 2 refuses a falling knife on the same logic it refuses a green spike, and nothing here has stopped going down yet.
entryWatch.why: Breadth is 10 red of 12 after six consecutive 10-green reads on Friday, and it is precisely the leaders being unwound: OKLO from +14.9% into Friday's bell to -7.7% now, SOUN +13.4% to -6.1%, IONQ +10.6% to -4.0%, SMR +3.0% to -4.8%, with QBTS -2.5%, MARA -4.0%, RGTI -1.1% and AMD -1.3% on a second red day. The fade that arrived too late to trade on Friday afternoon has arrived properly. None of it is buyable today: a one-day give-back of 4-8% inside a complex-wide unwind is not the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook buys, it is the first day of one, and buying into it is the averaging-down shape docs/RULES.md names as a setup that does not fit. The list below is carried at live 09:46 bids so the board is accurate, not because any of it is a candidate. UPST at -2.2% is the least damaged and is ranked second-best on the board precisely because it has no catalyst at all - which is an honest description of the field this entry was chosen out of.

candidatesAsOf: 2026-08-10 09:46 ET, live session bids struck by the open run about sixteen minutes into the session. The Last column is the official 8/7 settled close. These are opening-session quotes rather than marks - the tape is still finding its level after a weekend reversal, and the option books are visibly wide because of it.
candidatesNote: The account is flat with 109.88 of settled cash and ONE SPECIFICATION IS LIVE: buy 12 JOBY at a 8.85 limit, forced on item 1, expiring 10:30 ET. Read the rest of this list as the field that entry was chosen out of, ranked rather than merely refused, because a forced entry described as a good one corrupts the record the mandate exists to test. Breadth is 10 RED of 12, a complete reversal of the six consecutive 10-green reads Friday produced, and the reversal is concentrated in exactly the names that led it: OKLO, SOUN, IONQ and SMR are giving back between 4% and 8%. Two names are green. SMCI is one, and it is refused on its own straddle - 14.2% implied on the 8/11 print, which no 8% stop survives - and it was the only name here with a forward catalyst, which is why item 1 could not be passed and why today's entry is forced. JOBY is the other, and it is the entry. Ranked behind it: UPST second, on the thin merit of being the least damaged red name, with no catalyst whatsoever and the unrepaired 8/5 volume reversal still against it; SOUN, SMR, OKLO, IONQ, QBTS, RGTI and MARA refused together as one-day give-backs inside a complex-wide unwind, which is the first day of a decline rather than the pullback that follows one; LEU and AMD unreachable at one share. Options were priced across this list before any thesis was built and refused on spread for a third consecutive session - the tightest of eight live quotes was 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling.

candidates.note: 32.52 bid, +4.5%, one of only two green names on a 10-red board and being bid up into tomorrow night's report. NO-FLY, and refused on the number rather than the story: the 8/14 32-strike straddle marks 4.56 against a 32.21 spot, a 14.2% implied move, and the rulebook's 8% stop sits entirely inside that - the bad case gaps through the stop rather than filling at it. Any 3-6 week option necessarily spans the print and is forbidden outright. The estimate re-verified live today is 0.88, correcting the 0.69 this board has carried since 8/7. The only name here with a catalyst ahead, which is exactly why its elimination forced today's entry.

8.82 bid against 8.84, +2.1%, through Friday's 8.72 high and one of two green names on the board. THE ENTRY, published forced on item 1. Day 3 of a post-earnings continuation: 8/6 was the reaction bar, gapping 7.80 to 8.15 and closing 8.23 on 49.4M shares against roughly 35M average, and 8/7 continued to 8.64. The equity spread is 0.02, or 0.23% of mark, against option books on this same name quoting 75-106% this morning. Twelve shares is 106.20 of 109.88 deployable. What it lacks is a catalyst inside the hold, and that is marked fail rather than dressed up as relative strength.

17.74 bid, -1.1%, the mildest decline among the quantum names and the closest thing on this board to unchanged. Reported 8/6 after the close, so its no-fly flag is spent. Holding up better than its peers is not a setup, and there is nothing here beyond an absence of selling.
477.03 bid, -1.3%, a second consecutive red session and the only large-cap here. One share is more than four times the account, so it is carried for breadth context rather than as a candidate.
189.19 bid, -1.1%, giving back a little of the day-3 recovery it was making on Friday. Unreachable regardless - one share is 172% of the account.

30.39 bid, -2.2%, and now back below both the 30.20 close and the 30.32 pre-earnings line the 8/6 attempt failed at. Ranked second on the board today, which says more about the field than about UPST: it is the least damaged of the red names and it has no catalyst at all, while the 8/5 reversal - an open at 34.595 to a 30.20 close on 12.3M shares against a 5.1M average - is still unrepaired.

20.23 bid, -2.5%, giving back Friday's reclaim of the 20 line without having lost it yet. It missed on 8/6 at -0.13 against -0.10 and has moved with the complex ever since. Falling with the group it rose with is confirmation there was never anything of its own here.

42.63 bid, -4.0%, unwinding the +10.6% it carried into Friday's bell. The old objection stands and today adds to it: one share is 39% of the account, and an 8% stop is 3.41 of room in a name that has just travelled 1.80 in a session.

9.68 bid, -4.0%, and the only name here making lower lows for a third consecutive session - it was the weakest name on Friday's green tape and it is weak again on a red one. A name that falls with the market and also falls without it is the wrong side of a long.

9.34 bid, -4.8%, and it has now lost the 9.505 8/5 high that the original thesis wanted reclaimed and that held for six straight reads on Friday. Not held - the 8/14 9.50 calls were closed 8/6 at 0.49 for -14.0%. The 9/11 contracts were quoted live this morning to test the spread finding rather than to re-enter: the 9.00c is 1.06 bid against 1.53 and the 9.50c is 0.84 against 1.21, both about 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling.

7.53 bid, -6.1%, the second-worst name on the board after leading it on Friday at +13.4%. This is the give-back the 8/6 refusal was originally right about, arriving two sessions after this board handed the point back. A 6% down day is not the pullback the rulebook buys - it is day one of a decline, and the difference is whether anything has stopped falling yet.

44.59 bid, -7.7%, the worst name on the board and the sharpest reversal on it - it went into Friday's bell at +14.9% on the best move of the week. The 8/7 refusal on item 2 was proved right within one session: the reaction bar was the high. Item 2 now refuses it from the other direction, and at 44.59 one share would still be 41% of the account.
